Hi Samir / Laura —

Thanks again for the call earlier — quick recap and next steps from our side. High-level takeaways: 

- FinLytics target (end-to-end, client->model->client): p95 <= 350 ms for the common short calls, p99 <= 700 ms.
- Workload shape: ~95% short calls (<=64 tokens), ~5% long-form (up to ~512 tokens) that stream results.
- Concurrency/throughput: sustained ~80 concurrent requests, spikes to ~180–200 for 2–3 minute windows.
- Streaming: real-time partial outputs required (chunked streaming, client expects updates every ~200 tokens / ~250 ms).

Action items we agreed:
1) Redwood to run a side-by-side perf run against your sample prompt set (we'll use a sandbox key and your prompt corpus). We will capture p50/p95/p99, cold vs warm starts, and streaming chunk latency.
2) FinLytics to share current-provider perf CSV and any service-side traces you can provide (especially for p99 spikes).
3) Schedule a POC perf run next week — Marcus (cc'd) will own the test harness.

I attached a brief perf run template and an example summary from a recent customer so you can see the fields we'll capture.

Next call: would Monday 6/29 work to review the results and go over SLA/rollout options?

Thanks,

Marissa — thanks for the recap, that matches what we discussed. A few clarifications and the numbers from our current provider: 

- Current provider observed (end-to-end): p95 = 820 ms, p99 = 2.3 s (these are averages over last 30 days for the primary model variant).
- Typical concurrency: baseline ~60 concurrent, with traffic bursts up to ~180 for short windows.
- Token distribution: ~95% <=64 tokens, ~4% 65–256 tokens, ~1% >256 tokens.
- Streaming: we rely on streaming; partial tokens are used in the UI to display progressive answers. We need chunk latency under ~300–400 ms on stream updates.
- Cold starts: we see occasional cold starts adding ~600–900 ms at the p99 tail (depends on model variant).

I'll attach the CSV export of recent latency runs and a small set of server-side traces for a couple of p99 incidents. We're looking for two outcomes from the POC: 1) demonstrate this p95/p99 improvement for the short calls, and 2) validate streaming chunk latency for the long sessions.

Monday 6/29 works for an executive review — send a calendar invite and we can slot 30–45 minutes.

Thanks for the context — looping in technical next steps from Redwood SRE/SE perspective. A few notes and asks so our perf run is apples-to-apples: 

- Test harness: we will replay your prompt corpus against both Redwood hosted endpoints and a matching model variant on your current provider (if you can provide credentials or allow us to call from our sandbox to your sample endpoints).
- Metrics we will capture: client->edge RTT, model inference time, streaming-chunk latency, time-to-first-byte (TTFB), and end-to-end. We will mark cold vs warm by clearing model caches and measuring steady-state.
- Concurrency profile: please provide a short script or a traffic profile (per-second ramp up) so we can reproduce the same burst patterns.
- Auth & headers: we'll need an API key for the sandbox (or a temporary signed URL) and the exact headers you send (x-client-id, trace-id pattern) so we can preserve trace continuity.
- Fallbacks: confirm whether you currently use any local caching or client-side fallbacks that would affect p99 (retries/backoff) — we want to avoid skewing the baseline.

Also: we'd like to validate streaming behavior by measuring chunk emit time for the first 200 tokens and then subsequent 200-token windows. Can you confirm the chunk size and desired inter-chunk SLA? Samir mentioned ~300–400 ms target for chunk updates.

If you can drop the prompt set and the traffic profile link into the Drive folder you shared, we'll schedule the run Friday (6/26) night PST and send results by Monday for the review.

—Marcus
